summary:
ECharts should stay the kit's only general chart engine. Nearly every Chinese dashboard template, low-code BI tool and Python wrapper is built on it (DataEase, GoView, iDataV, BigDataView, and pyecharts 2.1, which now targets ECharts 6). The kit already pins echarts 6.1.0, so a second engine (G2 or VChart, +300–600 KB gz each) adds little.

The most useful finding is the official @echarts-x/* custom series (Apache-2.0, 2026-01). Each is a self-registering classic script of 2–15 KB that works from file://:
- bar-range gives a proper football-field chart.
- line-range covers ranges, fans and bands.
- violin, contour, segmented-doughnut and stage cover distributions, progress and timelines.
- word-cloud and liquid-fill replace the old ecomfe plugins, which still only support ECharts 5.

ECharts 6 features worth using:
- Design-token themes and runtime chart.setTheme() for light/dark.
- The matrix coordinate system for small multiples.
- Broken axes (verified working on 6.1).
- Automatic label anti-overlap.
- The 6.1 tooltip XSS fix.

One gotcha: ECharts candlesticks default to red-up / green-down (the Chinese convention). The kit needs a locale setting for this.

Security: the AntV npm namespace (and echarts-for-react) was compromised on 2026-05-19 by the "Mini Shai-Hulud" worm, which published 600+ malicious versions, all higher than the real latest versions. I verified the bad versions now return 404. The kit should pin exact versions, keep vendoring via npm pack (no install scripts), and record an integrity hash for each vendored file.

Pivot tables with subtotals are the one area where a Chinese library adds something the kit lacks. AntV S2 (302 KB gz, global S2) and VisActor VTable (531 KB gz; includes PivotChart and Gantt) are both MIT. Either is worth considering as a lazily loaded module, with Tabulator kept for flat tables.

For the future local-LLM step, the libraries themselves are poor bets:
- VMind is unmaintained; its repo is now VisActor/skills.
- LIDA has been stale since 2024 and works by executing Python code.
- AVA v4 has become a server-side Node framework.
- AntV's MCP chart server and Sive send data to hosted services.

What carries over is a pattern that GPT-Vis, VSeed, the echarts-mcp README and Chinese practitioners on Juejin all agree on. The LLM only fills in a minimal, schema-checked spec (chart type, dataset, dimensions, measures). A fixed compiler owns all styling, and charts are rendered before the text streams out. Our data/spec layer should follow VSeed's dimensions/measures shape. AntV T8-style inline number tags are a good fit for commentary boxes.

Chinese "data big-screen" style is not suitable for IB reports. That includes dark navy backgrounds, neon glow, glassmorphism, SVG tech borders, 3D, flying lines, liquid gauges, word clouds and 1920×1080 scale-to-fit. Worth borrowing: a restrained KPI count-up, linked highlighting, top-to-bottom storyline layout, the annotation vocabulary, and token discipline. VChart's veODesignLightFinance palette (navy/tan/oxblood) and tw93/Kami (paper background, one ink-blue accent) are good style references.

Xiaohongshu could not be read: search needs a login and signed API calls, and it is not indexed by the available search engines. Zhihu returned 403 and CSDN bodies are behind a script check. Community signals therefore come from Juejin (search API plus about 12 articles), Sogou WeChat search and CSDN titles.

libraries.name: Apache ECharts
libraries.capabilities: 40+ series (bar/line/scatter/candlestick/heatmap/sankey/treemap/sunburst/graph/geo/chord/beeswarm), dataset+transform, dataZoom, brush, visualMap, connect; v6: token-based themes, setTheme(), matrix coordinate system, broken axis, reusable custom series, label anti-overlap
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/echarts.min.js (global echarts); theme/*.js are UMD and register on the global; no runtime network calls
libraries.reason: Already the kit's core engine, and the Chinese ecosystem standard. v6 adds exactly the features pitchbooks need (matrix small multiples, broken axis, runtime themes). Keep NOTICE. Override candlestick red-up default.
libraries.size: 359 KB gz (1095 KB raw); simple build 164 KB gz
libraries.interactions_animation: dataZoom, brush, legend filtering, connect() for linked highlight and cross-filter, roam; setTheme without re-init; universal transitions
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: visualMap (color/size/opacity), symbolSize callbacks, symbol shape, polar/radial, geo + scatter bubbles, matrix layouts

libraries.name: @echarts-x custom series (bar-range, line-range, violin, contour, segmented-doughnut, stage, word-cloud, liquid-fill)
libraries.latest_version: bar-range 1.2.1 / line-range 1.1.1 / violin 1.1.1 / contour 1.2.1 / word-cloud 1.0.1 / liquid-fill 1.0.2
libraries.capabilities: Official reusable ECharts 6 custom series: range bars (football field), range lines/bands (fan charts), violin, contour, segmented doughnut, stage timeline, plus maintained word cloud and liquid fill
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/<name>.auto.min.js self-registers after echarts.min.js; use series {type:'custom', renderItem:'<name>'}
libraries.reason: Tiny (2-15 KB), official Apache project, permissive license, file://-safe. bar-range gives a proper football-field chart and line-range covers bands. They also replace the unmaintained ecomfe wordcloud/liquidfill plugins.

libraries.name: echarts-gl
libraries.capabilities: 3D globe, bar3D, scatter3D, surface, flowGL, scatterGL/linesGL for very large point sets
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/echarts-gl.min.js extends the global echarts; peer ^5.1.2 || ^6
libraries.reason: 3D distorts magnitudes and prints poorly, a big-screen idiom. Only scatterGL/linesGL for over 100k points is defensible.

libraries.name: echarts-wordcloud / echarts-liquidfill (legacy ecomfe plugins)
libraries.license: ISC (wordcloud, per package.json; no LICENSE file) / MIT (liquidfill)
libraries.capabilities: Word cloud; liquid-fill gauge
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/*.min.js; liquidfill dist assumes global self
libraries.reason: Unmaintained, peerDependencies echarts ^5 only, superseded by @echarts-x/custom-word-cloud and custom-liquid-fill. Both chart types have low information density for IB.

libraries.name: pyecharts
libraries.capabilities: Python fluent API emitting ECharts 6 options + HTML (supports v6 custom charts)
libraries.offline_classic_script: Output references CDN assets.pyecharts.org/assets/v6 by default; set CurrentConfig.ONLINE_HOST for local
libraries.reason: Good model for builder ergonomics and analyst prototyping. But it merges options, data and HTML and uses a CDN, which breaks the kit's separation of HTML, JS and data.

libraries.name: AntV G2
libraries.capabilities: Grammar of graphics (marks, transforms stackY/dodgeX/bin, facetRect, repeatMatrix, spaceFlex), interactions (brushFilter, legendFilter, sliderFilter), keyframe storytelling animation
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/g2.min.js (global G2), g2.lite.min.js
libraries.reason: Elegant grammar and facets, but it would duplicate ECharts at +320 KB gz. Its namespace was compromised on 2026-05-19 (malicious 5.5.8/5.6.8). Borrow grammar and facet ideas only.

libraries.name: AntV S2
libraries.capabilities: Canvas pivot (PivotSheet) and detail (TableSheet) tables, row/col totals and subtotals, frozen panes, tree mode, drill-down, sort/filter, copy/export, mini-chart cells
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/s2.min.js (global S2), self-contained; s2-extends.min.js optional
libraries.reason: Best fit for bank-style cross-tabs with subtotals, which Tabulator lacks. Load it lazily only where needed. Pin exactly (namespace incident; malicious 2.8.1/2.9.1 removed).
libraries.interactions_animation: Sort, filter, drill-down, hover highlight, scroll
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Rows x columns x values hierarchy; conditional color/bars in cells

libraries.name: AntV G6
libraries.capabilities: Graph visualization: force/dagre/combo/tree/mindmap layouts, plugins, 3D extension
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/g6.min.js (global G6)
libraries.reason: Only needed if ownership or holding-structure graphs become a core module. ECharts graph/tree covers simple cases. Compromised namespace.

libraries.name: AntV L7
libraries.capabilities: WebGL geospatial layers (point/line/polygon/heatmap/hexagon) on AMap/Baidu/Tencent/Tianditu/Google/Mapbox/MapLibre or blank Map
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/l7.js (global L7), but the logo control and some textures load from gw/mdn.alipayobjects.com; basemap adapters need keys and network
libraries.reason: WebGL-only (print risk), CDN fetches and online basemaps. Leaflet plus ECharts geo already cover proportional symbols and choropleths.

libraries.name: AntV X6
libraries.capabilities: Diagram/graph editor (flowcharts, ER, DAG)
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/x6.min.js (global X6)
libraries.reason: An editor is overkill for static client reports; static SVG diagrams suffice.

libraries.name: AntV AVA
libraries.capabilities: v3: ChartAdvisor (rule-based recommendation + chart lint), LiteInsight (trend/outlier/change-point). v4: Node 'AI-native Visual Analytics' (ai-sdk, DuckDB, ClickHouse)
libraries.offline_classic_script: v3 yes: dist/ava.min.js (global AVA); v4 is server-side
libraries.reason: Chart-lint rules are a good idea for QA of generated charts. But v3 has been stale since 2024 and v4 is a server framework in beta.

libraries.name: AntV G2Plot
libraries.capabilities: High-level charts on G2 4
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/g2plot.min.js
libraries.reason: Legacy, superseded by G2 5; namespace incident.

libraries.name: AntV GPT-Vis
libraries.capabilities: 26 LLM-friendly chart types via JSON or markdown-like ```vis DSL; streaming render (isVisSyntax), fault tolerant; themes default/dark/academy
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/umd/index.min.js (global GPTVis); no network calls found
libraries.reason: The DSL plus streaming plus fault-tolerance pattern is what step 2 needs. But the 649 KB gz bundle (G2+G6+T8) and the compromised namespace argue against using it as a runtime dependency.

libraries.name: AntV Infographic
libraries.capabilities: Declarative infographic engine, ~200 templates, SVG output, editor, streaming-tolerant syntax for LLMs, hand-drawn styles
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/infographic.min.js (global AntVInfographic), BUT fetches icons from weavefox.cn API and Alibaba PuHuiTi fonts from assets.antv.antgroup.com at runtime
libraries.reason: Interesting for exec-summary graphics, but its runtime CDN and API calls break offline use, the style skews towards casual PPT, and the namespace was compromised.

libraries.name: AntV T8 (narrative text visualization)
libraries.capabilities: Markdown with data-entity annotations, e.g. [¥1.2m](metric_value, origin=1234567); semantic +/- coloring, inline mini charts; LLM prompt templates
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/t8.min.js (global T8), no network calls
libraries.reason: Ideal for IB commentary boxes and LLM-generated narrative with data-bound numbers. It is only 18 KB gz. Pin and verify the hash (AntV namespace), or re-implement the entity syntax.

libraries.name: AntV mcp-server-chart + chart-visualization-skills + Sive
libraries.capabilities: MCP tools generating 25+ chart types, returned as image URLs from hosted GPT-Vis-SSR; agent skills for G2/G6/X6/GPT-Vis/Infographic/T8; Sive is a hosted AI analysis SaaS (repo is README-only)
libraries.offline_classic_script: No (Node/hosted services)
libraries.reason: By default data leaves the machine (hosted SSR, sive.antv.antgroup.com). Useful only as a template for how to structure skills and evaluations.

libraries.name: VisActor VChart
libraries.capabilities: Spec-driven charts with strong narrative features (rich markers, player/timeline, race charts, sequence animation), partial updateSpec, cross-platform/SSR; Finance themes via vchart-theme
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: build/index.min.js (global VChart), no network calls
libraries.reason: High quality and actively maintained, but it is a 617 KB gz second engine. Borrow its annotation and player ideas plus the veODesignLightFinance palette.
libraries.interactions_animation: Rich enter/update animation, player, race, cross-chart linking

libraries.name: VisActor VTable (+ vtable-gantt, vtable-sheet)
libraries.capabilities: Canvas ListTable/PivotTable/PivotChart (VChart charts per cell = small multiples), tree, frozen columns, sparkline/progress cells, editing, aggregation, autoWidth; Gantt and spreadsheet spin-offs
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/vtable.min.js (global VTable); PivotChart needs VChart registered
libraries.reason: The strongest Chinese table component, with very fast large-data rendering and charts in cells. It is heavier than S2 (531 KB gz, plus 617 KB if VChart is needed), so treat it as the alternative pivot engine and load it lazily.
libraries.interactions_animation: Sort, filter, drag columns, edit, hover/selection
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Pivot dims x measures; conditional style; charts in cells

libraries.name: VisActor VMind
libraries.capabilities: LLM chart generation, data extraction from text, dialog editing, insights (alasql, jsonrepair, OpenAI-compatible URL)
libraries.offline_classic_script: Partial: build/index.min.js (global VMind) but the UMD factory expects Node module globals (util/stream/http/fs)
libraries.reason: Repo renamed to VisActor/skills, whose README says the VMind SDK is no longer maintained. Helper package @visactor/calculator has no license field.

libraries.name: VisActor VSeed / VBI
libraries.capabilities: Business-semantic chart DSL (chartType, dataset, dimensions[{id,alias}], measures[{id,alias,parentId}]) compiled by Builder.from(vseed).build() to VChart/VTable specs; ~40 types incl. pivot and race; powers the Coze VisActor chart skill
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/umd/index.js (global VSeed, root=globalThis)
libraries.reason: The best model for our data/spec layer and for constraining LLM output, but it compiles to VChart rather than ECharts and is pre-1.0. Mirror its shape, don't depend on it.

libraries.name: VisActor VStory / VGrammar
libraries.capabilities: Data storytelling player (scenes, characters, animation) / low-level grammar
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes (global VStory / VGrammar)
libraries.reason: Pre-1.0; VStory is 1 MB gz and inactive since 2026-04.

libraries.name: @visactor/vchart-theme
libraries.capabilities: Theme JSONs: light/dark, arco, semi, veODesign Light/Dark x Finance/Government/Medical/..., vScreen big-screen themes (FinanceYellow, VolcanoBlue...)
libraries.offline_classic_script: public/*.json data files; build/index.min.js 17 KB
libraries.reason: The veODesignLightFinance palette (#294C60 navy, #E2B890 tan, #9D0800 oxblood, #324BCC royal, #9CADC8 slate) is the most pitchbook-like Chinese preset. Borrow the palette, not the library.

libraries.name: DataV (DataV-Team) / datav-vue3
libraries.capabilities: Big-screen Vue components: animated SVG borders, decorations, digital flop, scroll board, flyline map, water level
libraries.offline_classic_script: No (Vue component libraries)
libraries.reason: Vue-bound and unmaintained (last commit 2023-07). The neon 'tech' styling is the opposite of the IB aesthetic.

libraries.name: Big-screen template repos (iGaoWei/BigDataView, yyhsong/iDataV, jackchen0120/vueDataV, dromara/go-view)
libraries.license: BigDataView: none (collected from web); iDataV: none; vueDataV: MIT; GoView: MIT
libraries.capabilities: 100+ static ECharts/jQuery big-screen templates (incl. finance/listed-company cockpits); GoView low-code Vue3 editor
libraries.offline_classic_script: Static HTML mostly (BigDataView/iDataV)
libraries.reason: There is IP risk (no license, assets collected from the web), the dark neon style does not suit IB, and the fixed 1920x1080 layouts can't be printed. At most, use them as examples of what not to do.

libraries.name: DataEase / SQLBot
libraries.capabilities: Open-source BI dashboards (ECharts/AntV) / text-to-SQL chat BI
libraries.offline_classic_script: No (server apps)
libraries.reason: Copyleft licenses (GPL-3.0; SQLBot adds logo-retention terms) are incompatible with commercial client deliverables.

libraries.name: Microsoft LIDA
libraries.capabilities: Python: data summary, goal generation, visualization code generation and execution (matplotlib/seaborn/altair), edit/explain/repair; supports HF local and OpenAI-compatible endpoints (vLLM)
libraries.offline_classic_script: No (Python)
libraries.reason: Stale since 2024-03, and it executes generated code (security risk). The summarize, then goals, then spec pipeline is still a useful reference for step 2.

libraries.name: apache/echarts-mcp
libraries.capabilities: MCP demo: minimal-parameter chart tool (bar/line/pie/scatter/funnel/tree/treemap/sunburst), server-side render, image uploaded to Baidu BCE
libraries.offline_classic_script: No (Node server)
libraries.reason: It confirms the minimal-parameters-plus-fixed-theme approach for LLM charting, but it is a demo and needs Baidu cloud storage.

libraries.name: chart.xkcd / cutecharts ('cute' chart styles)
libraries.capabilities: Hand-drawn xkcd-style line/bar/pie/radar/scatter (cutecharts = Python port)
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes (UMD)
libraries.reason: Sketchy rendering looks unserious and imprecise in IB deliverables. I could not identify a 'Kitten' chart library.

libraries.name: tw93/Kami (document design system)
libraries.license: MIT (code); fonts mixed: TsangerJinKai personal-use only
libraries.capabilities: Agent design system for print documents incl. Equity Report template; tokens: parchment #f5f4ed, single ink-blue accent #1B365D, serif hierarchy, 'no gradients, no drop shadows, no 3D'
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a (HTML/PDF via WeasyPrint)
libraries.reason: A highly starred Chinese-dev example of restrained, print-first typography that suits pitchbooks. Do not bundle its TsangerJinKai font (not licensed for commercial use).

libraries.name: Source Han Sans / Noto Sans SC (CJK font)
libraries.capabilities: Pan-CJK sans in 7 weights; pairs with Inter for Latin/tabular numerals
libraries.offline_classic_script: Font files (subset to WOFF2 at build time with fonttools)
libraries.reason: The only safe, permissive CJK sans for Chinese-language deliverables. Avoid Alibaba PuHuiTi, HarmonyOS Sans and MiSans (custom licenses) and TsangerJinKai (personal use only). Full fonts are 8-16 MB, so subset per report.

key_insights: Security: on 2026-05-19 the 'Mini Shai-Hulud' worm hijacked npm account 'atool' and published 600+ malicious versions across 317-324 @antv/* packages, plus echarts-for-react, size-sensor and timeago.js. The bad versions were numbered above the real latest (e.g. g2 5.5.8/5.6.8 vs real 5.4.8), so any ^ range would have pulled them in. I verified they now return 404. Kit rules: exact pins, npm pack only (no lifecycle scripts), and a stored dist.integrity sha512 plus per-file sha256 checked by tools/vendor.py --check.

Adopt the official @echarts-x/* custom series (Apache-2.0, 2026-01). Each dist/<name>.auto.min.js is a 2-15 KB classic script that self-registers after echarts.min.js and works from file://; use it as series {type:'custom', renderItem:'bar-range'}. bar-range gives a native football-field chart and line-range covers bands and fan charts. violin, contour, segmented-doughnut and stage are also available. word-cloud and liquid-fill replace the unmaintained ecomfe plugins (peer echarts ^5).

ECharts 6 has a token theme system (lib/visual/tokens.js: neutral00-99, accent05-95, semantic aliases such as axisSplitLine and primary/secondary text) and chart.setTheme() for runtime switching without re-init. Generate both the CSS custom properties and echarts.registerTheme('ib-light'/'ib-dark'/'ib-print') from one token JSON.

Gotcha: ECharts candlestick defaults are red up (#eb5454) and green down (#47b262), the Chinese convention (红涨绿跌). Western IB readers expect the reverse. Add a convention token ('western'|'cn') that drives candlestick, waterfall and delta colours.

ECharts 6 matrix coordinate system: any series or component (grid, pie, heatmap, geo) can be placed in a table-like cell layout. Use it for think-cell-style peer panels and small multiples before reaching for VTable PivotChart or G2 facets.

ECharts 6 breaking changes to remember: the default theme and legend position changed (theme/v5.js restores them); geo/graph center percent base changed (legacyViewCoordSysCenterBase); rich text now inherits label style (richInheritPlainLabel:false); axis label anti-overflow is on by default (grid.outerBoundsMode:'none' to disable). 6.1.0 fixes a tooltip XSS in the lines series.

Pivot tables with subtotals are the one capability gap a Chinese library fills: AntV S2 2.7.2 (global S2, 302 KB gz, finance-style cross-tabs) or VisActor VTable 1.26.8 (global VTable, 531 KB gz, plus PivotChart charts-in-cells, which also needs VChart at +617 KB). Load either lazily, only on pages that need it. Keep Tabulator for flat tables.

AI chart generation consensus (GPT-Vis DSL, VSeed, the echarts-mcp README, Juejin '零幻觉交付' post): the LLM fills in only a minimal intent spec (chartType + dataset + dimensions/measures); a deterministic compiler owns style; JSON is validated and repaired; charts are pre-rendered and revealed during pseudo-streaming. Design the kit's spec now in VSeed's shape: dimensions[{id,label}], measures[{id,label,format,unit,parentId}], encodings, annotations.

VMind is dead: its repo was renamed to VisActor/skills, whose README says the VMind SDK is no longer maintained (npm frozen at 2.0.10, 2025-08). LIDA has been stale since 2024-03 and executes generated Python. AVA v4 is a Node framework. AntV's mcp-server-chart and Sive send data to hosted services. For step 2, copy the patterns, not the libraries.

Skills packaging pattern to copy for step 2 (VisActor/skills, antvis/chart-visualization-skills): SKILL.md + local references + templates + scripts + eval cases; the host agent supplies the model through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Note that VisActor-generated HTML loads from unpkg, and the storytelling skill uses GSAP (not an OSI license).

AntV T8 inline-entity syntax ([12.3%](delta_value, assessment=positive)) is an excellent, LLM-friendly format for IB commentary boxes with data-bound, consistently formatted numbers (18 KB gz). Vendor it pinned or re-implement it in the text-block component.

Offline traps in Chinese libraries: AntV Infographic fetches icons from www.weavefox.cn and Alibaba PuHuiTi fonts from assets.antv.antgroup.com at runtime. L7's logo control and textures load from alipayobjects.com, and its basemaps need AMap/Baidu/Tianditu keys. pyecharts defaults to the assets.pyecharts.org CDN. VisActor skill HTML loads from unpkg. The VMind UMD expects Node globals.

Maps: ECharts has not shipped china.json or world maps since v5. Never fetch boundaries at runtime from geo.datav.aliyun.com. China-facing deliverables may need officially approved national boundaries (审图号 / 'problem map' rules), so make the boundary dataset swappable per client jurisdiction. Flag for legal review.

Big-screen (数据大屏) idioms to reject for IB: dark navy backgrounds, neon (#00f5d4/#00bbf9/#9b5de5/#f15bb5), glow and gradients, glassmorphism, DataV SVG tech borders, 3D (echarts-gl), flying lines, liquid gauges, word clouds, auto-scrolling tables, 1920x1080 scale-to-fit (autofit.js). Ideas to borrow: a single restrained KPI count-up, linked highlighting, top-to-bottom/left-to-right storyline layout, markLine/markArea/markPoint annotations, token discipline.

Palette references: VChart veODesignLightFinance (#294C60 navy, #E2B890 tan, #9D0800 oxblood, #324BCC royal, #9CADC8 slate, #AD7F45 bronze) is the most pitchbook-like Chinese preset. tw93/Kami (paper #f5f4ed, a single ink-blue #1B365D accent, 'no gradients, no drop shadows, no 3D') matches the print-first IB look. GPT-Vis 'academy' is Tableau-10.

Feishu dataviz guide rules worth encoding as lint checks: line charts at most 5 series; pie under 9 categories; funnel at most 12 steps; area at most 3 series unless stacked; dual Y axes only for different units; legend bottom-centre on desktop and hidden for a single series; space priority marks > legend > axes > gridlines; avoid rotated labels.

Chinese fonts: only Source Han Sans / Noto Sans SC (OFL) is safe to bundle; subset per report with fonttools because full CJK fonts are 8-16 MB. LXGW WenKai and Smiley Sans are OFL but stylistically wrong for IB. Alibaba PuHuiTi, HarmonyOS Sans and MiSans use custom licenses, and TsangerJinKai is personal-use only. Support 万/亿 compact formatting for zh-CN (Intl.NumberFormat notation:'compact').

Xiaohongshu is not crawlable. Search needs a login and signed x-s API calls, the server-rendered page holds only shell strings, and site:xiaohongshu.com returns nothing in the available search engine. Zhihu returns 403 and CSDN bodies sit behind a script check. Juejin works (its search API plus a proof-of-work page check that a browser solves automatically), as does Sogou WeChat search. Many 2025-26 CSDN posts are AI-generated SEO content and some Juejin posts are marketing with false claims, so treat them as popularity signals only.
